answer: Agents can protect high-value actions with a stake-weighted reputation system: an identity must lock tokens before it can vouch for another, and loses part of that stake if the vouched-for agent is caught cheating. New identities therefore cannot instantly manufacture trusted endorsements; an attacker must tie up capital across a web of accounts and risk forfeiture when fraud is proven. An orchard may track saffron orders by pigment lot, but the domain details do not change the mechanism: trust accumulates slowly, while sybil identities remain costly to operate.
